record.paper_title: Open questions for strongly interacting Fermi gases with zero-range interactions
record.original_question: Can the finite-wave-number collective mode in the broken-pair continuum of a pair-condensed Fermi gas—the Andrianov-Popov or Higgs-like continuum branch with complex energy zq—be experimentally observed, and can its complex dispersion relation be measured precisely? The relevant excitation frequency is above the pair-breaking threshold, and zero-wave-number experiments do not access the finite-q continuum mode because its spectral weight vanishes as q approaches zero.

evidence.quote: There is therefore a collective mode in the continuum, which decays exponentially in time through the emission of broken pairs.
The observation of the continuum mode (at q > 0) and the precise measurement of its dispersion relation zq therefore remain to be done

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a three-dimensional pair-condensed Fermi gas of two spin states with attractive zero-range (s-wave) interactions, described in the BCS–BEC crossover by a mean-field-like superfluid order parameter Δ. Within RPA-type linear response, the modulus-modulus (and modulus-density) response functions of the order parameter possess, in addition to the gapless Anderson–Bogoliubov phonon branch, a collective excitation branch lying inside the broken-pair (pair-breaking) continuum 2Δ ≤ ω. This branch — the Andrianov–Popov / "Higgs-like" continuum mode — has a complex dispersion relation z_q (with Re z_q above the pair-breaking threshold and Im z_q < 0, encoding exponential decay through emission of broken pairs) and is reached by analytic continuation of the response function through its branch cut to the appropriate Riemann sheet.

A salient feature is that the spectral weight of this continuum mode in the response functions vanishes as q → 0, so that long-wavelength (q = 0) probes such as uniform interaction-strength modulation do not access it; finite wave number q > 0 is required.

Problem: Devise an experimental protocol on ultracold trapped Fermi gases at unitarity (or across the BCS–BEC crossover) that:
(i) selectively excites the finite-q Andrianov–Popov continuum branch with sufficient spectral weight to be detectable above the pair-breaking continuum background, and
(ii) yields a precise quantitative measurement of the complex dispersion relation z_q (both its real part — the resonance frequency — and its imaginary part — the intrinsic damping rate) as a function of the wave number q and of the interaction parameter 1/(k_F a_s).

Equivalently: prove or disprove that such a measurement is feasible with state-of-the-art cold-atom techniques, and if feasible, determine the optimal range of q and interaction strength for the observation.
artifact.category_tag: Collective modes in superfluid Fermi gases
artifact.status_search_result: Theoretical work establishes the Andrianov–Popov "Higgs-like" continuum branch with complex dispersion z_q and predicts it should be accessible to cold-atom experiments. Recent experiments (e.g., Phys. Rev. Lett. 133, 150403 (2024); Sci. Rep. 2023) measured the q ≈ 0 Higgs mode via interaction modulation, but a finite-q observation resolving the complex dispersion relation z_q has not been reported. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Collective excitation branch in the continuum of pair-condensed Fermi gases
status_evidence.snippet: The Popov-Andrianov-Higgs resonance is a robust, generic feature... should be accessible to state-of-the-art cold atom experiments.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical prediction; experimental observation at finite q proposed but not yet performed.

status_evidence.title: Exciting the Higgs Mode in a Strongly Interacting Fermi Gas by Interaction Modulation, PRL 133, 150403 (2024)
status_evidence.snippet: Periodically modulating the interaction strength and studying resonance frequency and line width.
status_evidence.claim: Recent experiments probe the q=0 Higgs mode, not the finite-q continuum dispersion.

status_evidence.title: Linear response of a superfluid Fermi gas inside its pair-breaking continuum
status_evidence.snippet: Resonance associated to Popov-Andrianov mode visible inside the pair-breaking continuum at all q.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical framework for finite-q complex dispersion.
